title: 第十五章鸮鸟第十六章连城第十七章窦氏
lines: 第十五章鸮鸟
长山县有个县令，姓杨，名令伯，此人贪得无厌，心狠手辣，是远近闻名的酷吏。他做官的唯一目的就是捞钱。谁送的钱多，谁就有理；谁不送钱，谁就没理。百姓恨之入骨，给他起了个外号，叫“杨刮地”——刮地皮的刮。
杨令伯手下有三个心腹，都是和他一样贪婪的人。一个叫周成，管刑狱；一个叫李贵，管钱粮；一个叫王德，管缉捕。这三人跟着杨令伯，坏事做尽，恶事做绝。百姓提起他们，没有不咬牙切齿的。
这一年秋天，杨令伯过寿。全县的乡绅、富户、商贾，都来送礼。礼单写了厚厚一本，金银财宝堆了满屋子。杨令伯坐在太师椅上，翘着二郎腿，一页一页地翻礼单，笑得合不拢嘴。
翻到最后一页，他忽然不笑了。那一页上写着一个人的名字——张福，本县的一个穷秀才，送了一匹布，一双鞋，还有一封信。
杨令伯打开信，看了一遍，脸色铁青。信里写道：“杨公大寿，本当重礼相贺。然学生家贫，无以为献，唯以布匹鞋袜聊表寸心。布虽粗，乃拙荆手织；鞋虽陋，乃老母亲做。望杨公笑纳。又及：近日乡间有鸮鸟夜啼，声甚凄厉，闻之不祥。学生窃以为，鸮鸟不祥，贪官亦然。愿杨公自省。”
杨令伯把信撕得粉碎，拍案大怒：“一个穷秀才，也敢骂我贪官？给我抓起来！”
周成、李贵、王德三人领命，带着一帮衙役，去了张福家。
张福家在三间破土房里，家徒四壁，穷得叮当响。他父亲早亡，母亲年老多病，妻子体弱，还有一个三岁的儿子。一家老小全靠他教书糊口，日子过得紧巴巴的。
张福正在屋里读书，听见外面吵吵嚷嚷的，出来一看，周成带着一帮衙役已经闯进了院子。周成冷笑一声，说：“张福，你胆子不小啊，敢骂县太爷？跟我们走一趟吧。”
张福的母亲颤颤巍巍地走出来，拉着周成的袖子，哭着说：“大人，我儿子是个老实人，他怎么会骂县太爷呢？一定是弄错了。”
周成一把甩开她，老太太摔倒在地，磕破了额头，血流了一脸。张福的妻子跑过来扶起婆婆，吓得浑身发抖。三岁的儿子躲在门后，哇哇大哭。
张福看着这一幕，眼睛红了。他握紧拳头，想冲上去，但他忍住了。他知道，冲上去也没用。他们人多，他打不过。他深吸一口气，说：“我跟你们走。”
周成让人把张福绑了，押着出了门。张福的母亲追到门口，哭着喊：“福儿，福儿！”张福回过头，看了母亲一眼，说：“娘，别担心，我没事。”他笑了笑，那笑比哭还难看。
张福被押到县衙，杨令伯升堂审问。他坐在太师椅上，翘着二郎腿，看着跪在堂下的张福，冷笑一声。
“张福，你可知罪？”
张福抬起头，看着杨令伯，说：“学生不知。”
杨令伯把撕碎的信扔在地上，说：“你骂本官贪官，还敢说不知？”
张福说：“学生没有骂大人。学生只是劝大人自省。鸮鸟不祥，贪官亦然——这话是古人之言，不是学生说的。学生只是引用。”
杨令伯气得脸都绿了，一拍惊堂木：“大胆！还敢狡辩！来人，给我打！”
衙役们按着张福，打了三十大板。张福咬紧牙关，一声不吭。打完了，杨令伯问：“你知罪了吗？”
张福趴在地上，嘴角流着血，说：“学生无罪。”
杨令伯大怒：“再打！”
又打了三十大板。张福还是不说。杨令伯气得浑身发抖，正要再打，周成凑过来，低声说：“大人，不能再打了。再打就出人命了。他是个秀才，打出人命来不好交代。”
杨令伯想了想，说：“把他关起来，等他想通了再说。”
张福被拖进了大牢。
张福在大牢里关了三个月。三个月里，他受尽了折磨。牢房里阴暗潮湿，老鼠成群，臭气熏天。他吃的是馊饭，喝的是脏水，睡的是烂草。他的伤口化脓了，发着高烧，浑身滚烫，人瘦得只剩一把骨头。
但他没有死。他活着，因为他不能死。他还有娘，还有妻子，还有三岁的儿子。他死了，她们怎么办？
他每天趴在牢房的地上，用手指在地上写字。写的是《论语》，是《孟子》，是他小时候背过的那些书。他写了一遍又一遍，写到手指磨破了，地上全是血，他也不停。他要记住那些字，记住那些道理。他是穷秀才，他什么都没有，但他有那些字，有那些道理。那些字告诉他，做人要堂堂正正，清清白白。那些道理告诉他，宁可穷死，不能屈死。
他在牢里待了三个月，杨令伯没有再审他，也没有放他。他像是被忘在了这里，像一块被扔进角落的破布。
有一天夜里，他做了一个梦。梦里他站在一座大殿前，殿很大，很空，只有一张桌子，桌上放着一本翻开的书。他走过去，看见书上写着字。他认识的字不多，但那些字他都能看懂。
上面写着他母亲的名字，写着她什么时候出生，什么时候嫁人，什么时候死了丈夫，什么时候养大了儿子。最后一行写着：“张门李氏，年六十三，思子成疾，当卒于三月十九。”
他抬头看墙上的日历。今天是三月十七。他的血一下子涌上头。他伸手去翻那本书，想翻到下一页，看看有没有转机。书页很沉，他翻不动。他用尽全身的力气，指甲都抠断了，书页还是一动不动。
他跪下来，磕头。磕了一个又一个，磕得额头都烂了，血流了一地。“求求你，求求你，让我出去，让我看看我娘。她不能死，她不能死。”
他磕了不知道多少个，磕到头都抬不起来了。他趴在地上，浑身发抖，像一片风中的枯叶。他听见一个声音，从很远的地方传来，像是风，像是水，像是有人在叹气。
“你回不去了。”
张福抬起头，看不见人，只有一道光，很亮，亮得他睁不开眼。“为什么？”
content_en:
Chapter 15 Owl
There was a magistrate in Changshan County, whose surname was Yang and whose name was Lingbo. He was greedy and ruthless, and he was known far and wide as a cruel official. His only purpose in becoming an official is to make money. Whoever gives more money will be justified; whoever doesn't give money will be ignored. The people hated him so much that they nicknamed him "Yang Guadi" - the scraper who scrapes the land.
Yang Lingbo has three confidants, all of whom are as greedy as him. One is named Zhou Cheng, who is in charge of punishment and prison; one is named Li Gui, who is in charge of money and food; the other is named Wang De, who is in charge of arrests. These three people followed Yang Lingbo and did all kinds of bad things. When people mention them, they all gnash their teeth.
In the autumn of this year, Yang Lingbo celebrated his birthday. All the squires, wealthy households and merchants from all over the county came to give gifts. The gift list was written in a thick volume, and the house was filled with gold and silver treasures. Yang Lingbo sat on the Taishi chair with his legs crossed, flipping through the gift list page by page, smiling from ear to ear.
Turning to the last page, he suddenly stopped smiling. There was a person's name written on that page - Zhang Fu, a poor scholar from this county. He gave a piece of cloth, a pair of shoes and a letter.
Yang Lingbo opened the letter and read it again, his face was ashen. The letter wrote: "I should congratulate Mr. Yang on his birthday. However, the student is poor and has nothing to offer, so he can only express his feelings with cloth shoes and socks. Although the cloth is thick, it is hand-woven by clumsy thorns; although the shoes are crude, they are made by the old mother. I hope Mr. Yang will accept it. Also: Recently, there is an owl in the countryside singing at night, and the sound is very sad and ominous. The students secretly believe that the owl is unlucky, and so are corrupt officials. May Mr. Yang reflect on himself."
Yang Lingbo tore the letter into pieces and was furious: "A poor scholar dares to accuse me of being a corrupt official? Arrest me!"
Zhou Cheng, Li Gui, and Wang De took the order and went to Zhang Fu's house with a group of government servants.
Zhang Fu's family lives in a three-room mud house with bare walls and is extremely poor. His father died young, his mother was old and sick, his wife was frail, and he had a three-year-old son. The whole family relies on his teaching to make a living, and their life is very tight.
Zhang Fu was studying in the house when he heard the noise outside. When he came out, he saw that Zhou Cheng and a group of government servants had broken into the yard. Zhou Cheng sneered and said, "Zhang Fu, you are very courageous. How dare you scold the county magistrate? Come with us."
Zhang Fu's mother came out tremblingly, pulled Zhou Cheng's sleeve, and cried, "Sir, my son is an honest man, how could he scold the county magistrate? He must have made a mistake."
Zhou Cheng threw her away and the old lady fell to the ground, breaking her forehead and bleeding all over her face. Zhang Fu's wife ran over and helped her mother-in-law up, trembling with fear. The three-year-old son was hiding behind the door, crying loudly.
Zhang Fu looked at this scene with red eyes. He clenched his fists and wanted to rush forward, but he held back. He knew that it would be useless to rush forward. There were so many of them that he couldn't defeat them. He took a deep breath and said, "I'll go with you."
Zhou Cheng had Zhang Fu tied up and escorted out of the house. Zhang Fu's mother chased her to the door, crying and shouting: "Fu'er, Fu'er!" Zhang Fu turned around, glanced at his mother and said, "Mom, don't worry, I'm fine." He smiled, and that smile was uglier than crying.
Zhang Fu was taken to the county government office, and Yang Lingbo went to court for interrogation. He sat on the Taishi chair, crossed his legs, looked at Zhang Fu who was kneeling in the hall, and sneered.
"Zhang Fu, do you know your guilt?"
Zhang Fu raised his head, looked at Yang Lingbo and said, "The student doesn't know."
Yang Lingbo threw the torn letter on the ground and said, "You accuse me of being a corrupt official, and how dare you say you don't know?"
Zhang Fu said: "The students did not scold the adults. The students just advised the adults to reflect on themselves. Owls are unlucky, and so are corrupt officials - these words are from the ancients, not from the students. The students just quoted them."
Yang Lingbo's face turned green with anger, and he was stunned: "How dare you! You dare to quibble! Come on, beat me up!"
The officials held Zhang Fu down and beat him thirty times. Zhang Fu gritted his teeth and remained silent. After the beating, Yang Lingbo asked, "Do you understand your crime?"
Zhang Fu lay on the ground, with blood streaming from the corner of his mouth, and said, "The students are not guilty."
Yang Lingbo was furious: "Hit me again!"
Hit thirty more boards. Zhang Fu still didn't say anything. Yang Lingbo was so angry that he was trembling all over. Just as he was about to hit him again, Zhou Cheng came over and whispered: "Sir, we can't hit him anymore. If we hit him again, he will be killed. He is a scholar, and it is difficult to explain why he killed someone."
Yang Lingbo thought for a while and said, "Lock him up and wait until he figures it out."
Zhang Fu was dragged into prison.
Zhang Fu was imprisoned for three months. For three months, he suffered a lot. The cell was dark and damp, infested with rats, and the stench was overwhelming. He ate rotten rice, drank dirty water, and slept on rotten grass. His wounds were suppurating, he had a high fever, his whole body was hot, and he was so thin that only a handful of bones remained.
But he didn't die. He lives because he cannot die. He also has a mother, a wife, and a three-year-old son. If he dies, what will they do?
Every day he lay on the floor of his cell and wrote on the ground with his fingers. What he wrote was "The Analects of Confucius" and "Mencius", which were the books he had memorized when he was a child. He wrote over and over again, and he didn't stop until his fingers were scratched and the ground was covered in blood. He wants to remember those words and those principles. He is a poor scholar, he has nothing, but he has those words and those principles. Those words told him that he should be upright and innocent. Those principles told him that he would rather die in poverty than die in submission.
He stayed in prison for three months, and Yang Lingbo neither tried him again nor released him. He seemed to be forgotten here, like a rag thrown into a corner.
One night, he had a dream. In the dream, he stood in front of a large hall. The hall was very large and empty. There was only a table with an open book on the table. He walked over and saw writing on the book. He didn't know many words, but he could understand those words.
Written on it was his mother's name, when she was born, when she married, when her husband died, and when she raised her son. The last line reads: "Mr. Li of Zhangmen, was sixty-three years old. She fell ill due to longing for her son and died on March 19th."
He looked up at the calendar on the wall. Today is March 17th. Blood rushed to his head. He reached for the book, wanting to turn to the next page to see if there was any improvement. The pages were so heavy that he could not turn them. He used all his strength, even his nails broke, but the page remained motionless.
He knelt down and kowtowed. Knocked one after another until his forehead was bruised and blood flowed all over the floor. "Please, please, let me out, let me see my mother. She can't die, she can't die."
He kowtowed so many times that he could no longer lift his head. He lay on the ground, shaking like a dead leaf in the wind. He heard a sound coming from far away, like wind, like water, like someone sighing.
"You can't go back."
Zhang Fu raised his head and saw no one, only a ray of light, so bright that he couldn't open his eyes. "Why?"
